heading_templates.section_headings: Question / Products or Services Involved / Instructions / Need More Help?
Issue/Question / Environment / Cause / Resolution / Clear the print queue via control panel / Clear the print queue via command prompt
Question / Products or Services Involved / Instructions / Need More Help? / ITS Staff Only

parsing_risks: PHASE 2 PARSING DECISION (not decided in Phase 1): an "ITS STAFF ONLY" section sits inside the body container in ['4535', '508', '233', '6260', '1866', '430', '9079']. It is publicly visible (human-checked logged out on 233) and is a list of links to technician articles. The body selector currently includes it. Likely handling: store it as a separate field rather than merging it into body text, so including or excluding it can be measured later.
3 article(s) use section headings other than Question/Answer or Issue/Environment/Cause/Resolution: ['4535', '5913', '9079']. Section-field mapping needs a rule for them.
No sample uses a Question/Answer pair: 'Question' appears only with 'Products or Services Involved / Instructions / Need More Help?', with no 'Answer' heading.
The Issue section is labelled 'Issue/Question' (a combined label), and 'Cause' is absent from some articles; the parser must treat both as normal.

Body text extracted with a space per element boundary (BeautifulSoup get_text(' ')) puts a space before punctuation that follows an inline tag, so the supplied phrase does not match in ['8721']. Phase 2 body extraction should not insert spaces at inline element boundaries (a, strong, em, span).

Body selector is an ASP.NET WebForms control ID (ctl00_ctl00_cpContent_cpContent_divBody). Stable across these samples, but a TeamDynamix upgrade could rename it; the collector's validity check should fail loudly when it matches zero or multiple elements.
Section headings are free-text panel titles written by KB authors, not a fixed schema; match them by normalized text, not by position.
Print pages carry no meta tags (no article:section, dates, or tags). Category and tags must come from the normal page.
category_conclusion: Each category page lists all of its direct articles in raw HTTP as plain <a> links with titles and summaries; the listing count equals the page's 'Articles (N)' header on every sample.
No pager elements and no page-query links. Pagination is not used: the full list is on one page.
Postbacks present only for: ['ctl00$ctl00$cpContent$cpContent$btnCategorySearch', 'ctl00$ctl00$cpContent$cpContent$btnToggleSubscribe'] (subscribe/search), not for listing or navigation.
Subcategories are plain <a href='/KB/Category/<id>/...'> links; their articles are NOT inlined, so full collection must walk subcategories recursively and dedupe article IDs.
Discovery looks stable enough for full collection with plain HTTP.
